The statement highlights stronger recent activity and a tight labor market, but stresses elevated inflation and ongoing policy tightening. Beige Book reports across Districts corroborate robust employment conditions: firms continue to hire, raise wages, and offer greater job flexibility to attract and retain workers, with broad wage growth noted. At the same time, businesses are facing and passing through higher energy costs (including fuel surcharges), and supply–demand imbalances—particularly in labor—remain a key source of price pressure. COVID developments, including China-related lockdowns, have disrupted supply chains and weighed on consumers in some areas, while the Russia–Ukraine war adds to cost pressures.

Against this backdrop, the latest SLOOS suggests credit conditions remain relatively supportive for many borrowers—easier standards for some C&I and consumer credit, lower line costs, and stronger business credit demand—even as residential real estate loan demand softens. Taken together, Beige Book and SLOOS signals imply near-term activity is still supported by strong labor markets and accessible credit, but inflation and cost pass-through keep risks skewed to the downside. Net effect: the outlook is slightly negative but closer to neutral than previously assessed.
